title_lines: Can you hear the difference between a Band 6 letter, and a Band 8 letter?
Today: a complaint about a damaged sofa. Same task. Same facts. Very different scores.
task: You recently bought a sofa from an online furniture store.
Write a letter to the company.
In your letter, describe what you ordered and what was wrong.
Explain how the problem has affected you.
Say what you want the company to do.

blocks: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to complain about the sofa I bought from your website last week.
My order number is 48213.
I ordered a grey three-seater sofa and it arrived on Friday.
However, when I opened the box, I saw that one leg was broken and there was a big mark on the front.
It also looks different from the photo on your website because the colour is much darker.
This problem has made me very upset.
I invited my family for dinner this weekend, so now I cannot use the sofa.
I also tried to call your customer service many times but nobody answered the phone, and this wasted a lot of my time.
I would like you to send me a new sofa as soon as possible.
If you can't do this, I want my money back.
Please reply quickly.
Yours faithfully,
Sam Taylor
flags: “Big mark” is basic. Band 8 names the problem precisely.
“Very” plus an adjective keeps the range limited.
A result in the present needs “I have invited” or “I had arranged”.
If you can't do this, I want my money back.
Contractions and blunt demands feel too informal.
verdict: The message is clear and all three bullets are answered.
Informal moments in a formal letter.
verdict_speech: It covers every point, and the message is clear.
But the vocabulary is basic and repeated.
The tone slips, and there are small errors.

blocks: Dear Sir or Madam,
I am writing to express my disappointment with the sofa I purchased from your website last week (order 48213), which arrived in an unacceptable condition.
I ordered a grey three-seater, and it was delivered on Friday.
Unfortunately, one of the legs had snapped off during transit, and a prominent stain ran across the front cushion.
Moreover, the fabric is noticeably darker than the colour shown online, so it does not match the product I chose.
This situation has caused considerable inconvenience.
I had arranged a family dinner for this weekend, and I now have nowhere for my guests to sit.
In addition, I attempted to contact your customer service team on several occasions, but nobody answered my calls, which only added to my frustration.
I would therefore be grateful if you could arrange for a replacement to be delivered by the end of next week.
Should this not be possible, I would expect a full refund.
I look forward to your prompt response.
Yours faithfully,
Sam Taylor
flags: States the reason at once, in a formal register.
A specific, natural pairing of words.
Links ideas smoothly without sounding mechanical.
nowhere for my guests to sit
Shows the effect instead of just saying “upset”.
I would expect a full refund.
Conditional language keeps the tone professional.
verdict: Every point is explained with detail.
Wide range, with only rare slips.
Polite, firm and easy to follow.
verdict_speech: Same facts. But now every point is fully developed.
The language is precise and natural.
And the tone is formal, polite, and firm.

upgrades.label: Tone
upgrades.band8: I would expect a full refund.
upgrades.speech: One. Tone. Instead of: I want my money back. Write: I would expect a full refund.

upgrades.label: Vocabulary
upgrades.speech: Two. Vocabulary. Replace: a big mark. With: a prominent stain.

upgrades.label: Linking
upgrades.band8: Moreover, the fabric is noticeably darker
upgrades.speech: Three. Linking. Swap the plain word also, for linkers like: moreover, and, in addition.

upgrades.label: Development
upgrades.band6: This problem has made me very upset.
upgrades.band8: I now have nowhere for my guests to sit.
upgrades.speech: Four. Development. Don't just say you were upset. Show the impact.
